reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Calling a syndrome TACI without all three components.
name: Oxfordshire Community Stroke Project Classification (Bamford)

version.label: OCSP / Bamford classification (Bamford et al. 1991)
version.detail: Four clinical syndromes. '-I' (infarct) is used when imaging confirms infarction; '-S' (syndrome) before imaging.

purpose: Classifies acute stroke by bedside clinical syndrome, which relates to lesion size, site and prognosis.
intendedPopulation: Patients with acute stroke, classified from the clinical examination.

inputDefinitions.label: Clinical syndrome

options.label: Total anterior circulation infarct
options.detail: All three: new higher cerebral dysfunction (e.g. dysphasia, neglect); homonymous visual field defect; ipsilateral motor and/or sensory deficit of at least two of face, arm and leg.

options.label: Partial anterior circulation infarct
options.detail: Two of the three TACI components, or isolated higher cerebral dysfunction, or a motor/sensory deficit more restricted than a lacunar syndrome (e.g. one limb, or face and hand).

options.label: Lacunar infarct
options.detail: Pure motor stroke, pure sensory stroke, sensorimotor stroke or ataxic hemiparesis, without higher cerebral dysfunction or visual field defect.

options.label: Posterior circulation infarct
options.detail: Ipsilateral cranial nerve palsy with contralateral motor/sensory deficit, bilateral motor/sensory deficit, conjugate eye movement disorder, cerebellar dysfunction without ipsilateral long-tract signs, or isolated homonymous visual field defect.

inputDefinitions.help: If the patient is drowsy or cannot be tested, higher cerebral dysfunction and field defect are often presumed present for TACI.

clinicalContext.text: A purely clinical classification that predicts lesion site, size and outcome.
Quick to apply at the bedside; frequently asked in examinations.

clinicalInsights.text: TACI carries the poorest prognosis of the four syndromes in the original cohort.
Lacunar syndromes do not always correspond to lacunar infarcts on imaging.

limitations.text: Clinical syndrome only; imaging may show a different lesion.

limitations: Assessment is harder in drowsy or aphasic patients.
Does not give stroke mechanism (see TOAST).

confounders.effect: Limits testing of cortical function and fields.
Can be mistaken for new features.

guideSections.what: Four clinical stroke syndromes: TACI, PACI, LACI and POCI.
guideSections.whenToUse: Bedside description of acute stroke; communication and prognosis.
guideSections.howToPerform: Examine for higher cerebral dysfunction, homonymous field defect, the distribution of motor and sensory deficit, and brainstem or cerebellar signs. Choose the syndrome that fits.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A clinical classification, used alongside imaging and TOAST.

sources.citation: Bamford J, Sandercock P, Dennis M, Burn J, Warlow C. Classification and natural history of clinically identifiable subtypes of cerebral infarction. Lancet. 1991;337(8756):1521-1526.
